## 2026-05-11 — session — γ.5 LXX integration (Month 3 #4, second translation joins KJV)

**Phases shipped:** γ.5 (LXX-Brenton-Greek translation
registered + Genesis 1:1-3 seed).
**Test delta:** +21 (`tests/test_lxx_gamma5.py`, 5 test
classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### What shipped

Three pieces register the LXX (Septuagint Greek) as a
discoverable translation:

1. **`content/translations/lxx-brenton-greek/_meta.yaml`**:
   ```yaml
   id: lxx-brenton-greek
   title: "Septuagint (Brenton, Greek text)"
   short_title: "LXX"
   license: "Public Domain"
   source:
     publisher: "Samuel Bagster & Sons (London)"
     source_date: 1844
   stats:
     books: 1
     verses: 3
   ```
   Explicit notes in the file call out the seed-vs-ETL
   handoff: γ.5 ships the wire-up + 3 canonical seed
   verses; γ.5.x is the corpus-wide ingest.

2. **`content/translations/lxx-brenton-greek/gen.py`** —
   Genesis 1:1-3 with the canonical LXX Greek text:
   - **Gen 1:1**: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸν οὐρανὸν
     καὶ τὴν γῆν. — the opening matches the NT
     prologue (John 1:1's Ἐν ἀρχῇ) by deliberate
     allusion, making this a particularly resonant seed.
   - **Gen 1:2**: distinctive LXX vocabulary —
     "ἀόρατος καὶ ἀκατασκεύαστος" (invisible and
     unformed) where the MT has "tohu wabohu". The
     LXX's Platonized rendering is itself an
     interpretive choice with centuries of patristic
     commentary built on it.
   - **Gen 1:3**: γενηθήτω φῶς, καὶ ἐγένετο φῶς.

3. **Tests** — 21 covering the discovery contract,
   metadata shape, seed verse content, and composition
   with γ.2's Greek lookup API.

### Discovery is filesystem-driven

The project's translation system (`scripts.core.translations`)
discovers translations by scanning `content/translations/`
at module load. Adding the new directory was sufficient
to make LXX appear in:
- `list_translations()` — returns
  `['kjv', 'lxx-brenton-greek']` post-γ.5.
- `/customize` console's popup-translation picker.
- `/compare` console's translation comparison panel.
- `api_customize_data()` + `api_publisher_data()` outputs.

No new API endpoints; no new console templates; no
edition-schema changes. The existing surfaces just pick
it up.

### Why a 3-verse seed (vs full Genesis)

Three verses prove the wire-up + give /compare a
working sample for the canonical opening. The full LXX
(~30 books, ~25,000 verses) requires sourcing from a
verified PD dump — currently candidates include:
- Brenton's complete 1844 edition scans on archive.org
  (image PDFs, would need OCR).
- The SEPTUAGINTA project (PD modern transcription).
- Rahlfs 1935 (rights-encumbered; the German Bible
  Society holds copyright — different translation id
  would be needed).

The seed quality is high (canonical, well-known text)
so the wire-up + Brenton attribution + PD claim are
verifiable. γ.5.x will tackle the ingest as a separate
session.

### Composition with γ.2 (Greek lookup)

The TestGamma5LxxComposesWithGreekLookup class pins
the future composition surface: the LXX text contains
words (e.g., ἀρχή = G746) that have full Strong's
Greek entries via γ.2's `/api/greek/<num>` endpoint.
A future γ.5.z feature can generate per-LXX-word
interlinear by joining LXX verse text against the
Strong's Greek lexicon — no new infrastructure needed,
just a JS-side feature on the /compare or /greek
console.

### Tests (21 new)

In `tests/test_lxx_gamma5.py`:

1. **TestGamma5LxxDirectoryLayout** (3 tests) — dir +
   _meta.yaml + gen.py all present.
2. **TestGamma5LxxMeta** (5 tests) — id, license=PD
   (drift guard against rights-encumbered LXX
   editions), short_title=LXX, Brenton 1844 attribution
   pinned (publisher / source_date), seed stats match
   shipped content.
3. **TestGamma5LxxDiscoverability** (5 tests) —
   `list_translations()` returns lxx-brenton-greek,
   `has_translation()` + `has_book(gen)` both true,
   `has_book()` false for unseeded books (pins the
   Genesis-only scope), `translation_meta()` returns
   the YAML data.
4. **TestGamma5LxxSeedVerses** (6 tests) — Gen 1:1
   opens "Ἐν ἀρχῇ", Gen 1:2 has the distinctive
   LXX "ἀόρατος" vocabulary, Gen 1:3 has γενηθήτω+φῶς,
   chapter returns 3 verses, unseeded verse returns
   None, every verse contains characters in the Greek
   Unicode range (U+0370-U+03FF or polytonic
   U+1F00-U+1FFF).
5. **TestGamma5LxxComposesWithGreekLookup** (2 tests)
   — γ.2's Greek lookup API still works post-γ.5
   (no module-import conflict), G746's lemma is ἀρχή
   (pinning that the future LXX-word-to-Strong's
   linking feature has data to work with).

### γ.5.x / γ.5.y / γ.5.z roadmap

Documented in this entry rather than as separate
phases (per the project's "letter slot stays sticky"
rule §5 — sub-versions stay under γ.5):

- **γ.5.x** — full LXX Greek corpus ingest from a
  verified PD source.
- **γ.5.y** — Brenton's English-side translation as
  `lxx-brenton-english` (separate translation id).
- **γ.5.z** — per-LXX-word link to `/api/greek/<num>`
  for interlinear rendering.

### What's next

Per Month 3 sequence:
- **Δ.12 FTS5 full-text search** — Δ.10's migration
  framework unblocked it. SQLite FTS5 virtual table for
  note bodies; ~10× faster than LIKE; phrase queries +
  snippets. ~1.5 sessions.
- **δ.1 reading streaks** — reader-side feature.
- **δ.2 bookmarks / highlights**.

Serial run: **2575 / 2576 tests pass (1 skipped); 11/11

## 2026-05-11 — session — γ.3 Patristic commentary kind (Month 3 #3, first content-depth phase to ship candidates)

**Phases shipped:** γ.3 (Patristic seed corpus +
`PatristicCommentary` loader + `PatristicCommentaryDetector`
+ ALL_DETECTORS registration).
**Test delta:** +21 (`tests/test_patristic_gamma3.py`,
4 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### Different shape from γ.1/γ.2

Where γ.1 (Hebrew) and γ.2 (Greek) shipped admin
consoles for looking up Strong's lexicon entries, γ.3
ships **content infrastructure** into the existing
prospect→promote note pipeline. No new console; no new
web route; instead a new detector that emits candidates
the user can promote into the live corpus via the
already-shipped `batch_promote_xrefs.py --kind comm-
patristic` flow.

### What shipped

Four pieces:

1. **`content/sources/patristic_commentaries.json`** —
   the seed corpus. 8 hand-curated Augustine-on-Genesis
   entries:
   - Gen 1:1 — "In the beginning" (Christological,
     Trinitarian reading) — *De Genesi ad litteram* I
   - Gen 1:2 — formless matter + Spirit hovering — *De
     Genesi ad litteram* I.4
   - Gen 1:3 — spiritual vs physical light — *De Genesi
     ad litteram* I.9
   - Gen 1:26 — Trinitarian "us" + image as rational
     soul — *De Trinitate* XII.7 + *De Genesi ad litteram*
     VI.12
   - Gen 2:7 — breath of life as direct soul-infusion —
     *De Genesi ad litteram* VII.1-3
   - Gen 3:1 — serpent as twisted-good (anti-Manichaean)
     — *De Genesi contra Manichaeos* II.14
   - Gen 3:6 — Fall as *defectus voluntatis* — *De
     civitate Dei* XIV.13
   - Gen 3:15 — protoevangelium read Christologically —
     *De civitate Dei* XVI.27

   **Honesty note**: each entry's `summary` field is a
   clearly-marked interpretive paraphrase, not a
   fabricated verbatim quote. The `_meta.scope` block
   in the JSON makes this explicit. Future γ.3.x can
   layer in actual quoted passages from the NPNF text
   dump once that ETL ships.

   Every entry cites NPNF Series 1 (Schaff, 1880s) with
   a PD marker — public-domain via Augustine's death
   (430 AD) + the 19th-century Schaff translations.

2. **`scripts/core/sources.py`** — `PatristicCommentary`
   frozen dataclass + `PatristicCommentaries` loader
   class. Mirrors the StrongsHebrew pattern:
   - `PATH = _SOURCES / "patristic_commentaries.json"`.
   - `__init__` raises `SourceMissingError` if the JSON
     is absent (defensive: the seed ships with γ.3 but
     a future "fetch" pipeline might separate it).
   - Indexes by `(book, chapter, verse)` for O(1)
     per-verse lookup AND by `father` for audit / future
     per-Father console.
   - `for_verse(book, chapter, verse)` → list of entries.
   - `by_father(name)` → list of entries.
   - Defensive: skips malformed entries silently
     (hand-edit typo protection).
   - `patristic_commentaries()` lru-cached factory.

3. **`scripts/core/detectors.py`** — `PatristicCommentaryDetector`
   class. Different shape from the keyword-matching
   language detectors:
   - `kind = "comm-patristic"`.
   - `detect(book, chapter, verse, verse_text)` does
     direct-lookup via `self.corpus.for_verse(...)` —
     no keyword matching needed; entries already
     verse-keyed.
   - Confidence **0.95** (curated PD content, not
     heuristic).
   - Body is an `<aside class="note-comm-patristic">`
     with `<strong>{father}</strong> <em>{work}</em>
     <small>(c. {year} AD)</small><p>{summary}</p>`.
   - All entry fields HTML-escaped via `html.escape()`
     for defensive XSS protection (curated content
     today, but future contributors might add untrusted
     entries).
   - Reviewer-notes flag the interpretive-summary
     framing: "substitute a verbatim quote from the
     NPNF dump where available".
   - Registered as the 8th entry in `ALL_DETECTORS`.

4. **No kind change** — `comm-patristic` was already
   declared in `content/kinds.yaml` (pre-γ.3 as an
   anticipated future-MVP slot, per the kinds-v2
   schema). γ.3 confirms the kind stays + tests pin
   its presence so a future kinds-cleanup can't drop
   it silently.

### How notes flow into the corpus

Today, after γ.3 ships:
1. Run `python scripts/prospect.py` — the
   PatristicCommentaryDetector runs over the corpus
   and produces 8 candidate `.json` files in
   `content/candidates/` (one per verse).
2. Review them in the editor (`python scripts/web.py`
   → `/` note-editor).
3. Promote with `batch_promote_xrefs.py --kind comm-
   patristic` — moves candidates → live notes in
   `content/notes/gen.py`.
4. Build an edition with `traditions_default` including
   `patristic` (the ψ.8 traditions filter) — the
   notes appear in the EPUB.

Promotion is a user-action (not auto), keeping the
publisher in control of which interpretive summaries
land in published editions.

### Tests (21 new)

In `tests/test_patristic_gamma3.py`:

1. **TestGamma3DataFile** (7 tests) — file exists,
   `_meta` block with required fields, entries list ≥5,
   every entry has all required fields, every entry
   cites NPNF + PD, Gen 1:1 present, seed is
   Augustine-only (explicit pin — if a future
   contributor adds another Father, they must update
   this test, forcing intentional scope expansion).
2. **TestGamma3PatristicCommentariesLoader** (6 tests)
   — frozen dataclass instances, by-verse lookup, empty
   list for verses without commentary, by-father lookup
   (Augustine = all), by-father empty for unknown
   (Origen not yet seeded), SourceMissingError when
   PATH is absent.
3. **TestGamma3DetectorContract** (6 tests) — registered
   in ALL_DETECTORS, kind == "comm-patristic", Gen 1:1
   emits Candidate with shape pinned (confidence 0.95,
   detector name, NPNF attribution, Augustine in body),
   empty list for uncommented verses, verse_text content
   irrelevant (direct-lookup, no keyword match), body
   HTML-escaped (synthetic entry with `<script>` proves
   the escape works).
4. **TestGamma3KindIsRegistered** (2 tests) — comm-
   patristic in kinds.yaml, has category=comm +
   label="Patristic".

### What γ.5 inherits

γ.5 LXX integration is the next Month 3 phase. It
composes with γ.2 (Greek lookup) and γ.3 (commentary)
naturally:
- The LXX is Greek OT text — each verse's Greek words
  can link to γ.2's `/api/greek/<num>` for per-word
  Strong's lookup.
- Patristic Greek commentary (Origen, Chrysostom,
  Basil) will compose with γ.3's seed Augustine
  set once γ.3.x extends the corpus.

### What's next

Per Month 3 sequence:
- **γ.5 LXX integration** — wraps the Septuagint text
  into the translation system. ~1 session.
- **Δ.12 FTS5 full-text search** — Δ.10's migration
  framework unblocked it. ~1.5 sessions.
- **δ.1 reading streaks** / **δ.2 bookmarks** —
  reader-side features.

### Test count

Serial run: **2554 / 2555 tests pass (1 skipped); 11/11
lint clean.** γ.2 baseline was 2533; +21 γ.3 = 2554.
Math checks out.

## 2026-05-11 — session — γ.2 Greek interlinear UI (Month 3 #2, mirrors γ.1's pattern)

**Phases shipped:** γ.2 (Greek lookup API + `/greek`
console + cross-link nav + lint route mapping +
test-isolation fix).
**Test delta:** +29 (`tests/test_greek_gamma2.py`,
5 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### What shipped

Five pieces wire a Strong's Greek lookup surface, mirroring
γ.1 with three intentional diffs:

1. **`scripts/api/greek.py`** — `api_greek_lookup(num)`.
   Direct mirror of `scripts/api/hebrew.py`:
   - Same input-normalization shape: `G1` / `g1` / `1`
     / `G0001` / `0001` all → canonical `G1`.
   - Same error envelopes: 400 invalid_format, 404
     unknown_number, 503 lexicon_missing.
   - Same response shape (number, lemma, xlit, pron,
     derivation, definition, kjv_def, attribution).
   - `StrongsGreekEntry.xlit` normalizes the upstream
     `translit` field — γ.1 and γ.2 consumers share
     rendering code.

2. **`scripts/templates/greek.py`** — `GREEK_HTML` console.
   Two intentional diffs vs HEBREW_HTML:
   - **LTR** (no `direction: rtl` on `.greek-lemma`) —
     Greek reads left-to-right.
   - **Conditional pron** — Greek lexicon entries
     usually lack a `pron` field; renderer guards
     `if (data.pron) { ... }`. Hebrew always renders it.
   Everything else identical: search form, result card
   built via `textContent` DOM construction, full ζ
   foundation via `<head>` markers, deep-link via
   `/greek#G3056`.

3. **`_design.CONSOLES`** extended — now 17 consoles
   total. The cross-link nav auto-propagates so every
   other console picks up `/greek` link, and `/greek`
   picks up every other console.

4. **`scripts/web.py`** — `GREEK_HTML` + `api_greek_lookup`
   imported; `if path == "/greek"` HTML branch added in
   `do_GET`; `(re.compile(r"^/api/greek/([Gg]?\d+)$"),
   api_greek_lookup)` registered in `_REGEX_GET_ROUTES`.

5. **`scripts/lint_rules.py`** — `route_for_constant`
   table extended with `"GREEK_HTML": "/greek"` so the
   §6.2 cross-link invariant check stays clean.

### Test-isolation fix (incidental, real)

The first full-suite run after γ.2 surfaced 7 test
failures in γ.2's API + data-sanity classes — all
reporting `Greek lexicon looks truncated; got 3 entries`
or `expected lemma to be non-empty`. Root cause:

```python
# tests/test_corpus_chi1.py — line 107-108:
monkeypatch.setattr(self.src.StrongsGreek, "PATH", cache_path)
self.src.strongs_greek.cache_clear()
```

The `monkeypatch.setattr` auto-reverts `StrongsGreek.PATH`
at test teardown, but the `lru_cache` on
`sources.strongs_greek()` retains the stale `StrongsGreek`
instance built from the tiny synthetic cache. Later tests
(γ.2's, alphabetically after `test_corpus_chi1`) get the
leftover tiny lexicon (1-3 entries) instead of the real
5,523-entry one.

**Fix**: γ.2's affected test classes call
`sources.strongs_greek.cache_clear()` in `setup_class`.
Mirrors what chi1 itself does at *its* own setup — chi1
clears the cache going IN; γ.2 clears it going IN too.
Defensive: future tests using `strongs_greek` should
follow the same pattern OR chi1 should also clear on
teardown.

γ.1 doesn't suffer this — chi1 only monkeypatches
`StrongsGreek.PATH`, never `StrongsHebrew.PATH`. The
asymmetry is preserved: γ.1's tests don't need the
defensive clear.

### Pattern validation

γ.2 is the second console built on the post-Month-2
foundation (γ.1 was the first). The pattern is now
proven repeatable:
1. New `scripts/api/<topic>.py` handler.
2. New `scripts/templates/<topic>.py` template + `<TOPIC>_HTML`
   constant + `apply_design_system` substitution.
3. `_design.CONSOLES` += one entry.
4. `scripts/web.py` += HTML route branch + regex route.
5. `scripts/lint_rules.py` += `route_for_constant` entry.
6. `tests/test_<topic>_<phase>.py` × 5 test classes
   (API, template, route reg, cross-link, data).

Future γ.3 / γ.5 (and beyond) will reuse this scaffold.

### Tests (29 new)

In `tests/test_greek_gamma2.py`:

1. **TestGamma2ApiLookup** (10 tests, +1 vs γ.1) —
   canonical/bare/lowercase/zero-padded G1, unknown
   → 404, bogus → 400, G0 → 400, full shape pinned,
   **λόγος (G3056) canonical example**, **ἀγάπη (G26)
   verifies Greek Unicode range** (U+0370–U+03FF).
   Setup_class clears the lru_cache.
2. **TestGamma2GreekTemplate** (9 tests, +1 vs γ.1) —
   valid doc, markers substituted, ζ foundation,
   **LTR (not RTL)** — explicit assert that
   `.greek-lemma` block lacks `direction: rtl`, lookup
   form, `/api/greek/` endpoint called (NOT
   `/api/hebrew/`), textContent escape, **conditional
   pron render** (`if (data.pron)`), hash deep-link.
3. **TestGamma2RouteRegistration** (3 tests) — HTML
   route in web.py, `api_greek_lookup` in
   `_REGEX_GET_ROUTES`, regex accepts G-prefixed +
   bare numbers, rejects bogus.
4. **TestGamma2CrossLinkPropagated** (5 tests) —
   `/greek` in CONSOLES, preflight nav has /greek,
   **`/hebrew` nav has `/greek` AND vice versa**
   (γ.1 + γ.2 are paired), `/greek` self-links to all
   16 other consoles.
5. **TestGamma2FullDataAvailable** (2 tests) — lexicon
   loads ≥5000 entries (the +29 tests subtract the test
   that's now the cache-clear setup_class), G1 + G3056
   + G26 all present. Setup_class clears the lru_cache.

### What γ.2.x inherits

Like γ.1.x for Hebrew, a future γ.2.x will wire Greek
data into `build_edition.py`'s popup pipeline so the
buyer-facing EPUB renders Greek interlinear inline with
NT verses. Same scope shape; ~1 session each.

### What's next

Per Month 3 sequence:
- **γ.3 Patristic commentary kind** — different shape
  (creates notes via existing detector pattern, not a
  new console). ~1 session.
- **γ.5 LXX integration** — wraps the Septuagint Greek
  OT text into the translation system. Composition
  with γ.2's Strong's Greek is natural — LXX text + per-
  word Strong's links.
- **Δ.12 FTS5 full-text search** — Δ.10 unblocked it.
- **δ.1 reading streaks** / **δ.2 bookmarks**.

### Test count

Serial run: **2533 / 2534 tests pass (1 skipped); 11/11
lint clean.** γ.1 baseline was 2504; +29 γ.2 = 2533.
Math checks out.

## 2026-05-11 — session — γ.1 Hebrew interlinear UI (Month 3 #1, first content-depth phase)

**Phases shipped:** γ.1 (Hebrew lookup API + `/hebrew`
console + cross-link nav + lint route mapping).
**Test delta:** +27 (`tests/test_hebrew_gamma1.py`,
5 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### Why this opens Month 3 cleanly

Month 2's modernization arc shipped a full ζ foundation
(theme tokens, dark mode, typography, icons, toasts,
skeletons, command palette). γ.1 is the first ship to
**compose all of it** for a real content-depth feature.
The Hebrew console gets dark mode, themable typography,
SVG icons, toast errors, and Cmd+K integration **for
free** — every ζ phase pays out here.

### What shipped

Four pieces wire a Strong's Hebrew lookup surface end-to-end:

1. **`scripts/api/hebrew.py`** — the JSON endpoint handler:

   ```python
   api_hebrew_lookup("H1")     → {"status": "ok", "number": "H1",
                                  "lemma": "אָב", "xlit": "ʼâb", ...}
   api_hebrew_lookup("1")      → same (normalizes bare → H-prefixed)
   api_hebrew_lookup("h1")     → same (case-insensitive)
   api_hebrew_lookup("H0001")  → same (strips leading zeros)
   api_hebrew_lookup("99999")  → {"status": "error", "code":
                                  "unknown_number", "http": 404, ...}
   api_hebrew_lookup("abc")    → {"status": "error", "code":
                                  "invalid_format", "http": 400, ...}
   ```

   Lazy-imports `scripts.core.sources` so the API module
   stays light to import. Surfaces `SourceMissingError`
   as a 503 with the install hint ("Run:
   python3 scripts/fetch_sources.py").

2. **`scripts/templates/hebrew.py`** — the `HEBREW_HTML`
   console. Search form (text input + button), result
   card rendering each lexicon field. Hebrew lemma
   renders RTL at 2.25rem; transliteration in mono;
   derivation / definition / KJV-usage as labeled
   sections; attribution footer.

   - **DOM construction (not innerHTML interpolation)** —
     every field uses `node.textContent = data.X` so any
     future entry containing exotic codepoints stays
     XSS-safe by construction.
   - **Composes the full ζ foundation** — markers for
     `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`, `DARK_MODE_JS`, `THEME_ICONS_JS`,
     `THEME_TOAST_JS`, `THEME_CMD_PALETTE_JS`,
     `BUYER_ARC_POLISH_CSS` all in `<head>`.
   - **Deep-link support** — `/hebrew#H7225` reads the
     hash, auto-populates the input, and triggers the
     lookup. Shareable URLs for citing specific Strong's
     entries.
   - **Graceful errors** — fetch failure surfaces via
     `window.ebibleToast(msg, 'error')` (ζ.6). 5xx
     responses also toast; 4xx renders the message
     inline in the result panel.

3. **`_design.CONSOLES` extended** with
   `("/hebrew", "hebrew")` — the 16th console. The
   cross-link nav auto-propagates to every other console
   via the `<!-- HEADER_NAV_LINKS -->` substitution; no
   per-template edit required.

4. **`scripts/web.py`** route registrations:
   - Import `HEBREW_HTML` (template) +
     `api_hebrew_lookup` (handler).
   - `do_GET` branch: `if path == "/hebrew" or path ==
     "/hebrew.html": return self._send_html(HEBREW_HTML)`.
   - `_REGEX_GET_ROUTES` entry:
     `(re.compile(r"^/api/hebrew/([Hh]?\d+)$"),
     api_hebrew_lookup)`.

5. **`scripts/lint_rules.py`** — `route_for_constant`
   table extended with `"HEBREW_HTML": "/hebrew"` so the
   §6.2 cross-link invariant check recognizes the new
   console.

### Scope choice (vs. building Hebrew-in-EPUB directly)

The "Hebrew interlinear UI" name could mean either an
admin console or buyer-facing inline Hebrew in the
built EPUB. γ.1 ships the **admin console + JSON API**
foundation; a future **γ.1.x** ships the build-pipeline
integration that injects Hebrew word data into OT
verse popups.

Reasons for splitting:
- The console surfaces the data publishers actually
  curate against — they can verify what's in the
  lexicon before committing to an interlinear strategy.
- The JSON API becomes the canonical Hebrew lookup
  service. γ.2 Greek mirrors this exact pattern; future
  build-pipeline integration consumes the same endpoint
  (or its in-process equivalent).
- γ.1.x can ship without re-thinking the data layer.

### Tests (27 new)

In `tests/test_hebrew_gamma1.py`:

1. **TestGamma1ApiLookup** (9 tests) — canonical H1,
   bare 1, lowercase h1, zero-padded H0001 all return
   ok with the same canonical number; unknown number →
   404; bogus inputs (abc / empty / 1.5 / H / Hxyz) →
   400; H0 → 400 (Strong's starts at 1); full response
   shape pinned; Genesis 1:1's H7225 returns Hebrew
   characters in `lemma` (catches lexicon-data
   truncation).
2. **TestGamma1HebrewTemplate** (8 tests) — valid HTML
   doc, every theme marker substituted, full ζ foundation
   present (tokens + dark mode + icons + toasts +
   palette + typography), Hebrew RTL rule, lookup form
   present, `/api/hebrew/` referenced in JS, label +
   xlit inserted via `textContent`, hash deep-link
   handler present.
3. **TestGamma1RouteRegistration** (3 tests) —
   `if path == "/hebrew"` in web.py, `api_hebrew_lookup`
   in `_REGEX_GET_ROUTES`, regex accepts H1/h1/1/H0001/
   8674 and rejects abc/empty/decimal.

## 2026-05-11 — session — ζ.8 command palette (Cmd+K) — Month 2 #7, **closes the modernization arc**

**Phases shipped:** ζ.8 (`window.ebibleCmdPalette` API +
CSS rules + /preflight retrofit + global Cmd+K listener).
**Test delta:** +30 (`tests/test_cmd_palette_zeta8.py`,
5 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### Month 2 closure

This ship closes the seven-phase **modernization arc**:

```
ζ.1 → ζ.2 → ζ.4 → ζ.5 → ζ.6 → ζ.7 → ζ.8
foundation  dark  type  icons toast skele  ⌘K
```

Each phase composed the earlier ones. ζ.8 sits at the
apex — uses **ζ.1** surfaces + accent, **ζ.4** body +
mono typography, **ζ.5** chevron-right icon. The
foundation pays maximum dividends here.

### What shipped

Four pieces wire a global command palette:

1. **`THEME_CMD_PALETTE_JS` constant** in `_design.py`
   (~180-line `<script>` IIFE, built via
   `_build_cmd_palette_js()` helper). Public API:

   ```js
   window.ebibleCmdPalette.open();    // open the palette
   window.ebibleCmdPalette.close();   // close it
   window.ebibleCmdPalette.toggle();  // toggle
   ```

   - **Keyboard binding**: a global `keydown` listener
     on `document`. Cmd+K (macOS via `metaKey`) or
     Ctrl+K (Windows/Linux via `ctrlKey`) toggles the
     palette from anywhere.
   - **CONSOLES list** is JSON-embedded into the JS at
     module load (same pattern as ζ.5's `THEME_ICONS_JS`).
     The Python `CONSOLES` tuple stays single source of
     truth.

2. **Modal contract**:
   - `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` +
     `aria-label="Command palette"`.
   - Result list: `role="listbox"`, rows
     `role="option"`, `aria-selected` toggled per item,
     `aria-activedescendant` on input points at the
     current row id.
   - Backdrop click closes (target check distinguishes
     backdrop click from modal-content click).
   - Esc closes; Enter opens selected; ↑/↓ navigate
     with `scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest'})`.
   - **Focus management**: snapshots
     `document.activeElement` on open, restores it on
     close — keyboard users don't lose context after
     dismissing.

3. **Search filter**:
   - Case-insensitive substring match on either `label`
     OR `route`.
   - Empty result set renders "No matches.".
   - First match auto-selected; selection resets to 0
     on every filter update.
   - Label + route inserted via `textContent` (XSS-safe).

4. **Palette CSS** added to `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`:

   - `.theme-cmd-backdrop` — fixed inset:0, z-index:9999,
     `rgba(15,23,42,0.5)` light + `rgba(0,0,0,0.65)` dark
     override, flex centering, 12vh top padding for
     visual rest.
   - `.theme-cmd-modal` — max-w 32rem, ζ.1 surface +
     text + border tokens, 20px shadow, max-h 70vh.
   - `.theme-cmd-input` — full-width, ζ.4 base-size
     body-font, no outline, bottom border (visual
     separator).
   - `.theme-cmd-list` — scrollable result panel,
     0.375rem padding.
   - `.theme-cmd-item` — flex row: label + mono-route +
     chevron-right icon.
   - `.theme-cmd-item-selected` — `--color-accent` bg +
     `--color-text-on-accent` text; icon opacity flips
     0→1.
   - `.theme-cmd-footer` — page-tint background with
     `↑↓ navigate · ↵ open · Esc close` hints rendered
     in `.theme-cmd-kbd` pills (small mono).
   - `@keyframes theme-cmd-fade-in` — 150ms fade.

### Why this matters beyond just "Cmd+K"

The project has 15 consoles. Pre-ζ.8 navigation was:
1. Visit any console
2. Find the cross-link nav in the header (15 links)
3. Click the right one

Post-ζ.8: hit Cmd+K from anywhere, type 2-3 letters,
hit Enter. Power-user workflow now matches the standard
established by VSCode / Slack / Linear / Figma.

The fact that 0 console templates besides /preflight
have absorbed the THEME_TOKENS_CSS marker yet — and Cmd+K
still works on /preflight — also demonstrates the
opt-in marker pattern is clean: a future console adding
the marker gets a fully-themed palette for free, no per-
console JS edits required.

In `tests/test_cmd_palette_zeta8.py`:

1. **TestZeta8CmdPaletteJs** (12 tests) — script wrapper,

   empty state.
2. **TestZeta8CmdPaletteConsoles** (3 tests) — JSON

3. **TestZeta8CmdPaletteCss** (8 tests) — backdrop has

## 2026-05-11 — session — ζ.7 skeleton loaders (Month 2 #6, themable + a11y-aware loading placeholders)

**Phases shipped:** ζ.7 (shimmer-animated skeleton CSS +
/preflight retrofit + a11y-aware aria-busy lifecycle).
**Test delta:** +14 (`tests/test_skeletons_zeta7.py`,
3 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### What shipped

Three pieces wire themable skeleton placeholders:

1. **Skeleton CSS** added to `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`:

   ```css
   .theme-skeleton {
     display: inline-block;
     background: linear-gradient(
       90deg,
       var(--color-bg-surface) 0%,
       var(--color-border) 50%,
       var(--color-bg-surface) 100%
     );
     background-size: 200% 100%;
     border: 1px solid var(--color-border);
     border-radius: 0.25rem;
     animation: theme-skeleton-shimmer 1.6s ease-in-out infinite;
   }
   .theme-skeleton-text  { display: block; width: 100%; height: 1em; }
   .theme-skeleton-block { display: block; width: 100%; height: 4rem; }
   @keyframes theme-skeleton-shimmer {
     0%   { background-position:  100% 0; }
     100% { background-position: -100% 0; }
   }
   @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
     .theme-skeleton { animation: none; }
   }
   ```

   The shimmer effect is a horizontal slide of the
   linear-gradient — the bright band (`--color-border`)
   sweeps left-to-right across the surface base
   (`--color-bg-surface`). `background-size: 200% 100%`
   gives the animation horizontal room to move.

   **A11y**: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables
   the animation entirely (WCAG 2.3.3). Vestibular-
   disorder users get a static block instead of a moving
   one.

2. **/preflight retrofit** — replaced the
   `<p class="text-slate-500 text-sm">running checks…</p>`
   placeholder with the proper loading state:

   ```html
   <div id="checks" class="space-y-2"
        aria-busy="true" aria-live="polite">
     <span class="sr-only">Loading preflight checks…</span>
     <div class="theme-skeleton theme-skeleton-block" style="height:3.5rem"></div>
     <div class="theme-skeleton theme-skeleton-block" style="height:3.5rem"></div>
     <div class="theme-skeleton theme-skeleton-block" style="height:3.5rem"></div>
   </div>
   ```

   Three stacked skeleton blocks mimic the eventual
   check-row layout. `aria-busy="true"` tells screen
   readers the section is loading; `aria-live="polite"`
   ensures the real content gets announced once it
   arrives. The `sr-only` (Tailwind utility) span carries
   the explicit loading message for assistive tech.

3. **JS lifecycle fixes** — both happy + sad paths now
   properly clear the loading state:

   ```js
   // renderChecks() — happy path (real data arrived)
   const root = document.getElementById('checks');
   root.innerHTML = '';
   root.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'false');  // ← ζ.7 added

   // loadPreflight catch block — sad path (fetch failed)
   root.innerHTML = '';                           // ← ζ.7 added: clear skeletons
   root.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'false');       // ← ζ.7 added: unblock SR
   if (window.ebibleToast) {
     window.ebibleToast('Failed to load preflight: ' + e.message, 'error');
   } else { /* graceful fallback to fail-bg div */ }
   ```

   Without these, screen readers would stay parked in
   "loading preflight checks…" forever after a fetch
   failure — a real a11y bug the toast-only ζ.6 fix
   didn't catch.

### Composition payoff

ζ.7 composes ζ.1 (surface + border colors) for the
shimmer and ζ.6 (toast error path) for the failure UX.
The skeleton themes correctly in dark mode automatically
because both shimmer colors come from `--color-*` tokens
that flip in `:root[data-theme="dark"]`.

### Tests (14 new)

In `tests/test_skeletons_zeta7.py`:

1. **TestZeta7SkeletonCss** (8 tests) — base rule
   present, uses `--color-bg-surface` + `--color-border`,
   uses `linear-gradient` + `background-size: 200% 100%`,
   uses `animation: theme-skeleton-shimmer`, text
   variant present (height: 1em), block variant present,
   `@keyframes` defined, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:
   reduce)` rule disables animation on `.theme-skeleton`.
2. **TestZeta7PreflightRetrofit** (5 tests) — old
   "running checks…" text removed, ≥3 skeleton-block
   placeholders, `#checks` has aria-busy="true" +
   aria-live="polite", sr-only "Loading preflight
   checks" message present, renderChecks clears both
   innerHTML and aria-busy.
3. **TestZeta7FetchErrorClearsSkeletons** (1 test) —
   the loadPreflight catch block (anchored on the
   function name, not the bare `} catch (e) {` which
   collides with the dark-mode-JS's localStorage catch)
   clears innerHTML, resets aria-busy, and calls
   ebibleToast.

### What ζ.8 inherits

ζ.8 command palette will be the closing Month 2 piece.
It can use:
- `--color-bg-surface` for the overlay + result panel.
- `--color-text-primary` for the search input.
- `--font-stack-mono` for code-style keyboard shortcut
  hints (e.g., `Cmd+K`).
- `window.ebibleIcons.chevron-right` for result-row
  affordance.
- `window.ebibleToast` for action-completion feedback.
- `.theme-skeleton-block` if results load async.

The full ζ foundation pays maximum dividends here.

**ζ.8 command palette (Cmd+K)** closes the Month 2
modernization arc. Then **Month 3 content depth wave 1**

## 2026-05-11 — session — ζ.6 toast notifications (Month 2 #5, first composed-foundation phase)

**Phases shipped:** ζ.6 (`window.ebibleToast` API + CSS
rules + /preflight error-path retrofit).
**Test delta:** +25 (`tests/test_toasts_zeta6.py`,
4 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### Why this is significant beyond just "toasts"

ζ.6 is the first ζ.* phase that **composes** three prior
foundations:
- **ζ.1** — `--color-status-{info,success,warn,error}` for
  per-kind chrome, `--color-bg-surface`/`--color-text-primary`
  for the base body (themes correctly in dark mode).
- **ζ.4** — `--font-size-sm` + `--leading-normal` for the
  toast body text.
- **ζ.5** — `window.ebibleIcons` for the leading status
  icon per kind.

If a future audit asks "did the ζ foundation actually
build into anything?" the answer is ζ.6 — every prior
phase pays dividends here.

### What shipped

Four pieces wire a centralized toast notification system:

1. **`THEME_TOAST_JS` constant** in `_design.py` —
   `<script>` block defining the public API:

   ```js
   window.ebibleToast(message, kind);
   // kind: 'info' | 'success' | 'warn' | 'error'
   //   (defaults to 'info' for unknown kinds)
   ```

   Implementation details:
   - **Container**: `<div id="ebible-toast-container">`
     lazy-created on first call. Class:
     `theme-toast-container`. Sits at `top: 4rem; right:
     0.75rem` (below ζ.2's dark-mode toggle).
   - **Auto-dismiss**: `AUTO_DISMISS_MS = 4000`. The
     timer cancels on mouseenter so users can read long
     messages.
   - **Manual dismiss**: × button with
     `aria-label="Dismiss notification"`.
   - **ARIA contract**: error kind → `role="alert"` +
     `aria-live="assertive"` (immediate screen-reader
     announcement). Others → `role="status"` +
     `aria-live="polite"` (announce at next idle).
   - **Icon dispatch**: pulls from `window.ebibleIcons`
     (ζ.5). info → info, success → check, warn →
     alert-triangle, error → x-circle.
   - **XSS guard**: message text inserted via
     `textContent`, not innerHTML. Caller doesn't need
     to escape user-controlled text.
   - **Unknown-kind defense**: `hasOwnProperty` guard
     falls back to info if `kind` doesn't match the four
     known values. A typo doesn't crash; it just renders
     a generic info toast.

2. **Toast CSS rules** added to `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`:

   - `.theme-toast-container` — fixed position, click-
     through via `pointer-events: none` (the toasts
     themselves re-enable pointer-events).
   - `.theme-toast` — base chrome: `--color-bg-surface`
     background, `--color-text-primary` text, 1px border,
     box-shadow, `--font-size-sm` size, slide-in
     animation.
   - `.theme-toast-{info,success,warn,error}` — per-kind
     border color + icon color from `--color-status-*`.
   - `.theme-toast-message` — flex: 1; word-wrap: break-
     word (so a long URL doesn't blow out the toast width).
   - `.theme-toast-dismiss` — × button styling, hover
     state, flex-shrink: 0.
   - `.theme-toast-leaving` — sets up the slide-out
     animation on dismiss.
   - `@keyframes theme-toast-in` — 200ms slide-in
     (opacity + translateX).
   - `@keyframes theme-toast-out` — 200ms slide-out
     (opacity + translateX, forwards).

3. **`<!-- THEME_TOAST_JS -->` marker** added to
   `apply_design_system`. Substitutes the constant when
   the marker is present; no-op otherwise.

4. **`/preflight` retrofit** — `loadPreflight`'s catch
   block migrated:

   ```js
   // before
   root.innerHTML = `<div class="fail-bg border p-4 rounded">failed to load: ${escapeAttr(e.message)}</div>`;

   // after
   if (window.ebibleToast) {
     window.ebibleToast('Failed to load preflight: ' + e.message, 'error');
   } else {
     // Graceful fallback — shouldn't fire in practice since
     // THEME_TOAST_JS is inline in <head>.
     root.innerHTML = `<div class="fail-bg border p-4 rounded">failed to load: ${escapeAttr(e.message)}</div>`;
   }
   ```

### Usage examples (for future console authors)

```js
window.ebibleToast('Edition saved.', 'success');
window.ebibleToast('Network error: ' + e.message, 'error');
window.ebibleToast('2 editions still need a popup translation.', 'warn');
window.ebibleToast('Build queued; refresh in 5s.', 'info');
```

No marker needed in console templates if `apply_design_system`
absorbs THEME_TOAST_JS for the template — `/preflight` is
the proof-of-concept. Other consoles can add `<!-- THEME_TOAST_JS -->`
to their `<head>` when they want toasts.

### Tests (25 new)

In `tests/test_toasts_zeta6.py`:

1. **TestZeta6ToastJs** (11 tests) — script wrapper,
   ebibleToast API exposed, four-kind dispatch with
   correct icon names, 4000ms auto-dismiss timer pinned,
   error → assertive + role=alert (others → polite +
   role=status), message via textContent (XSS-safe),
   container id pinned, container creation idempotent,
   dismiss button has descriptive aria-label, unknown
   kinds fall back via hasOwnProperty, hover pauses
   auto-dismiss (mouseenter + clearTimeout).
2. **TestZeta6ToastCss** (7 tests) — container rule
   (fixed + pointer-events: none), base toast rule
   references ζ.1 color vars + ζ.4 size var, four
   per-kind rules exist, each kind references its
   `--color-status-<name>` var at least twice (border +
   icon), dismiss button has flex-shrink: 0, leaving
   animation rule, both @keyframes (in + out).
3. **TestZeta6ApplyDesignSystem** (3 tests) — marker
   substitution, no-op on missing marker, idempotency.
4. **TestZeta6PreflightWired** (4 tests) — marker
   substituted, ebibleToast present in rendered HTML,
   error path calls ebibleToast with 'error' kind +

- Use `--color-bg-surface` as the skeleton base color

## 2026-05-11 — session — ζ.5 iconography pass (Month 2 #4, replaces /preflight unicode glyphs with themable inline SVGs)

**Phases shipped:** ζ.5 (inline-SVG icon registry + JS
exposure + `.theme-icon` utility + /preflight retrofit).
**Test delta:** +25 (`tests/test_iconography_zeta5.py`,
6 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### What shipped

Five pieces replace /preflight's unicode-glyph status
icons (✓ ⚠ ✗) with proper inline SVGs that inherit
`currentColor` and scale via parent font-size:

1. **`ICONS_REGISTRY: dict[str, str]`** in
   `scripts/templates/_design.py` — 6 Lucide-shape icons
   used by /preflight today (and future ζ.6/7/8 phases):
   - `check` — pass status (replaces ✓)
   - `alert-triangle` — warn status (replaces ⚠)
   - `x-circle` — fail status (replaces ✗)
   - `info` — informational banners (ζ.6 toasts will use)
   - `chevron-right` — disclosure indicator
   - `external-link` — outbound-link visual hint

   Each icon is built via `_make_icon(name, path)` which
   wraps the Lucide path in the canonical SVG attrs:
   24x24 viewBox, 2px stroke, `stroke="currentColor"`,
   `fill="none"`, `aria-hidden="true"`, `class="theme-icon"`,
   `data-icon="<name>"` for DOM inspection.

2. **`theme_icon(name)` Python builder** — returns SVG
   markup for known icons, empty string for unknown
   names (graceful degrade on typos rather than raising,
   so a template typo doesn't crash the page).

3. **`THEME_ICONS_JS` constant** — `<script>` block
   exposing the registry as `window.ebibleIcons`. The
   payload is JSON-encoded so the SVG strings'
   double-quotes (`stroke="currentColor"` etc.) don't
   break the JS literal. Generated at module load — any
   future addition to `ICONS_REGISTRY` automatically
   appears in `window.ebibleIcons` without separate
   maintenance.

4. **`.theme-icon` utility class** in `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`:

   ```css
   .theme-icon {
     display: inline-block;
     width: 1em;
     height: 1em;
     vertical-align: -0.125em;
     flex-shrink: 0;
     stroke: currentColor;
     fill: none;
   }
   ```

   SVG sizes to 1em of parent's font-size; stroke + fill
   inherit via `currentColor`. The `-0.125em` vertical-
   align tweak puts the icon on the text baseline rather
   than the cap-height.

5. **`<!-- THEME_ICONS_JS -->` marker substitution**
   added to `apply_design_system`. /preflight absorbed
   the marker in `<head>` between `DARK_MODE_JS` and
   `BUYER_ARC_POLISH_CSS`. JS migrated:

   ```js
   // before
   icon.textContent = '✓';
   icon.className = 'text-3xl pass';
   const icon = {pass: '✓', warn: '⚠', fail: '✗'}[status];

   // after
   function statusIconHtml(status) {
     const name = {pass: 'check', warn: 'alert-triangle', fail: 'x-circle'}[status];
     return (window.ebibleIcons && window.ebibleIcons[name]) || '';
   }
   icon.innerHTML = statusIconHtml(status);
   icon.className = `text-3xl ${status}`;
   ```

### Why a registry + JSON exposure

The pattern needed by /preflight (JS-driven banner icon)
diverged from the simpler "Python f-string embed" pattern.
Some surfaces are server-rendered (HTML strings produced
in Python) — they use `theme_icon(name)`. Others are
client-rendered (DOM nodes built by inline JS) — they use
`window.ebibleIcons[name]`. Both consume the same single
source-of-truth `ICONS_REGISTRY`.

JSON-encoding the payload sidesteps a class of bug where
naïve string interpolation of SVG into a JS literal
breaks on the SVG's internal double-quotes
(`stroke="currentColor"` etc.) The JSON encoder handles
escaping correctly. `JSON.parse` happens implicitly via
the JS engine consuming the embedded object literal.

### Cascade caveat (icons-specific)

Unlike ζ.2's body-text fix where conflicting Tailwind
classes had to be removed, icons don't have the same
collision — Tailwind's CDN doesn't ship an `.icon` class.
The `.theme-icon` rule lands cleanly. (The /preflight
banner-icon span retains its `text-3xl` Tailwind class to
provide the font-size CONTEXT that the SVG's `1em` sizing
consumes — that's not a collision, it's parent-to-child
inheritance.)

In `tests/test_iconography_zeta5.py`:

1. **TestZeta5IconsRegistry** (8 tests) — 3 required
   status icons present (check, alert-triangle, x-circle),
   3 utility icons present (info, chevron-right,
   external-link), every entry is a valid SVG element,
   every entry uses `stroke="currentColor" fill="none"`,
   every entry uses `viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, every entry
   carries `aria-hidden="true"`, every entry carries
   `class="theme-icon"`, every entry records its name
   via `data-icon` attribute.
2. **TestZeta5ThemeIconHelper** (2 tests) — returns

3. **TestZeta5ThemeIconsJs** (3 tests) — `<script>`
   wrapper, exposes `window.ebibleIcons`, payload parses

4. **TestZeta5ThemeIconUtilityClass** (4 tests) — rule

   alignment.
5. **TestZeta5ApplyDesignSystem** (3 tests) — marker

ζ.6 toasts can now:

## 2026-05-11 — session — ζ.4 typography upgrade (Month 2 #3, themable type scale)

**Phases shipped:** ζ.4 (typography tokens + utility
classes + body rule + /preflight retrofit).
**Test delta:** +18 (`tests/test_typography_zeta4.py`,
4 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### Slot note: ζ.3 was not allocated

`PROPOSAL_FEATURE_LANDSCAPE.md` §6 Month 2 sequence goes
ζ.1 → ζ.2 → **ζ.4** → ζ.5 → ζ.6 → ζ.7 → ζ.8. The ζ.3 slot
was never assigned a phase. Per §5 sticky rule it stays
unassigned (and reserved for any later "I want this
between dark mode and typography" candidate, if one ever
materializes). Today's ship claims ζ.4 — no number is
being skipped, just the proposal's gap respected.

### What shipped

Three pieces extend ζ.1's `THEME_TOKENS_CSS` with a
themable typography layer:

1. **Typography tokens added to `:root`** (theme-
   independent — font choice doesn't change between light
   and dark, so no `:root[data-theme="dark"]` override
   needed):

   ```
   --font-stack-body   ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont,
                       "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, "Noto Sans",
                       sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji"
   --font-stack-mono   ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas,
                       "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace
   --font-size-xs      0.75rem    (12px)
   --font-size-sm      0.875rem   (14px)
   --font-size-base    1rem       (16px)  ← anchor
   --font-size-lg      1.125rem   (18px)
   --font-size-xl      1.25rem    (20px)
   --font-size-2xl     1.5rem     (24px)
   --leading-tight     1.25
   --leading-normal    1.5
   --leading-relaxed   1.625
   --font-weight-normal     400
   --font-weight-medium     500
   --font-weight-semibold   600
   --font-weight-bold       700
   ```

2. **`body { ... }` rule added to `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`** —
   sets `font-family`, `font-size`, `line-height` from the
   tokens. Tailwind v3 CDN's preflight sets `font-family`
   on `html`; the more-specific selector winning the
   cascade is `body`, so this rule wins for the entire
   DOM tree without per-element migration.

   ```css
   body {
     font-family: var(--font-stack-body);
     font-size: var(--font-size-base);
     line-height: var(--leading-normal);
   }
   ```

3. **11 new utility classes** consume the tokens:

   - `.theme-text-xs` / `.theme-text-sm` / `.theme-text-base`
     / `.theme-text-lg` / `.theme-text-xl` / `.theme-text-2xl`
     (each pairs font-size + line-height — smaller sizes
     use `leading-normal`, larger sizes use `leading-tight`)
   - `.theme-font-mono` (font-family swap for code/pre)
   - `.theme-weight-normal` / `.theme-weight-medium`
     / `.theme-weight-semibold` / `.theme-weight-bold`

### Font-loading decision

System stack only — no Google Fonts, no Bunny CDN, no
external dependency. Reasons:
- Zero network cost (the modern stack resolves to the OS
  default sans-serif: SF Pro on macOS, Segoe UI on
  Windows, Roboto on Android, Inter-like on Chromium 84+
  via `ui-sans-serif`).
- No FOIT / FOUT — fonts paint on first render.
- Matches the project's "no build step" rule
  (CLAUDE_PROJECT_RULES §6.3).
- Future opt-in is one token edit: swap
  `--font-stack-body` to `'Inter', ui-sans-serif, ...` +
  add a `<link>` for Inter, and every console picks it up.

### `/preflight` retrofit

```html
<!-- before -->
<h1 class="text-2xl font-semibold mb-2">...</h1>
<p class="text-sm text-slate-600 mb-6">...</p>
<style>.details-list { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; ... }</style>

<!-- after -->
<h1 class="theme-text-2xl theme-weight-semibold mb-2">...</h1>
<p class="theme-text-sm theme-text-muted mb-6">...</p>
<style>.details-list { font-family: var(--font-stack-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); ... }</style>
```

The Tailwind utility-class removal pattern from ζ.2 (drop
`text-2xl` / `font-semibold` rather than augment) is
applied here too: leaving the Tailwind classes alongside
the theme classes would let the CDN's JIT-injected
utilities win the cascade.

The `.details-list` font-family change uses the var()
fallback chain so consoles that haven't absorbed
`THEME_TOKENS_CSS` still get the original `ui-monospace`
stack — backward-compatible.

### Cascade caveat (same as ζ.2)

Tailwind CDN injects utility classes AFTER inline
`<style>` blocks; same-specificity utilities WIN. The
fix for typography is identical to ζ.2's: REMOVE
conflicting Tailwind classes when migrating to
`theme-*`. The `body { ... }` rule works because it
targets `body` directly (not via a class), and Tailwind's
preflight targets `html` — different element, no
specificity collision.

### Tests (18 new)

In `tests/test_typography_zeta4.py`:

1. **TestZeta4TypographyTokens** (6 tests) — font-stack-body
   token present + uses `ui-sans-serif` + `system-ui`,
   font-stack-mono present + uses `ui-monospace`, six-step
   size scale present, base size is `1rem`, three leadings
   present, four weights present.
2. **TestZeta4TypographyUtilities** (5 tests) — six
   `.theme-text-*` classes present, each references its
   `var(--font-size-*)` lookup, each pairs line-height,
   `.theme-font-mono` references `--font-stack-mono`, all
   four `.theme-weight-*` classes present.
3. **TestZeta4BodyFontRule** (3 tests) — `body { ... }` rule
   present, references `var(--font-stack-body)`, sets
   base size + leading.
4. **TestZeta4PreflightRetrofit** (4 tests) — h1 uses
   `theme-text-2xl theme-weight-semibold`, body
   paragraphs use `theme-text-sm`, `.details-list` uses
   themable mono var (with rgb fallback chain), no
   residual Tailwind `text-2xl` on the h1.

### What ζ.5 inherits

ζ.5 iconography pass now has a stable type-scale to size
icons against. The toggle button SVG from ζ.2 already
uses `width="18" height="18"` (hardcoded). ζ.5 can
introduce a `.theme-icon` utility sized via
`--font-size-base` (or a dedicated `--icon-size-*` set),
plus a small inline-SVG icon library (Lucide-shape: 24x24
viewBox, 2px stroke). The /preflight pass/warn/fail
unicode glyphs (✓ ⚠ ✗) are candidates for SVG promotion
in ζ.5.

palette (Cmd+K).

## 2026-05-11 — session — ζ.2 dark mode (Month 2 #2, first user-visible payoff of the modernization arc)

**Phases shipped:** ζ.2 (dark-mode toggle activating
ζ.1's `:root[data-theme="dark"]` block).
**Test delta:** +20 (`tests/test_dark_mode_zeta2.py`,
3 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### What shipped

Four pieces wire dark mode end-to-end:

1. **`DARK_MODE_JS` constant** added to
   `scripts/templates/_design.py` (alongside ζ.1's
   `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`). It's a `<script>` block
   intended to be placed inline-blocking in `<head>`,
   not deferred. The order matters: the script must
   execute BEFORE the body paints so dark-mode users
   never see a flash of light (FOAUC).

2. **Synchronous init** at script-load:
   - Read `localStorage.getItem('ebible_theme')` —
     namespace-prefixed key to avoid collision with
     future per-feature toggles.
   - Fall back to `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-
     scheme: dark)')` for first-time visitors.
   - Default to light.
   - `setAttribute('data-theme', 'dark')` or
     `removeAttribute('data-theme')` accordingly.

   This runs ~10ms before the rest of the page paints.
   localStorage access is wrapped in try/catch so
   private-mode browsers degrade to media-query-only
   rather than throwing.

3. **`window.ebibleTheme` public API** — exposed for
   tests + future ζ.* components:
   ```js
   window.ebibleTheme.get()         // 'dark' | 'light'
   window.ebibleTheme.set('dark')   // applies + persists + dispatches
   window.ebibleTheme.toggle()      // flips current
   ```
   Each `set` dispatches a `themechange` CustomEvent on
   `document` with `{ detail: { theme } }`, so future
   ζ.6 toasts / ζ.7 skeletons / chart-redraw code can
   listen and adapt.

4. **Toggle button** inserted on `DOMContentLoaded`:
   - Fixed position (`top: 0.75rem; right: 0.75rem;
     z-index: 9999`) — no console-markup edits needed.
   - Sun/moon SVG icons (inline; ~5 lines each) swap
     based on active theme.
   - `aria-label="Toggle dark mode"` for screen
     readers.
   - Idempotent: checks for existing `#ebible-theme-
     toggle` before inserting (safe against double
     DOMContentLoaded firings).
   - Button's own background/color adapt to the active
     theme via inline styles, so it stays visible on
     consoles that haven't yet absorbed `THEME_TOKENS_CSS`.

5. **`apply_design_system` extended** to substitute
   `<!-- DARK_MODE_JS -->`. Mirrors the existing
   `<!-- THEME_TOKENS_CSS -->` and
   `<!-- BUYER_ARC_POLISH_CSS -->` patterns. Idempotent;
   no-op when marker absent.

6. **`/preflight` retrofit** (the proof-of-concept
   console already wired for ζ.1):
   - Marker `<!-- DARK_MODE_JS -->` added in `<head>`
     between `THEME_TOKENS_CSS` and `BUYER_ARC_POLISH_CSS`.
   - `<body class="bg-slate-50 text-slate-800">` →
     `<body class="theme-bg-page theme-text">`. The
     Tailwind classes were REMOVED (not just augmented)
     because Tailwind CDN's JIT-injected utilities
     otherwise win the cascade and dark mode wouldn't
     visibly toggle.
   - Header migrated to `theme-bg-surface theme-border`.
   - Corpus-progress badge migrated to `theme-text-muted`.

### Cascade caveat (worth pinning for ζ.4+)

Tailwind v3 CDN compiles utilities at JS runtime and
injects styles into `<head>`. Those injected styles
come AFTER inline `<style>` blocks (including
`THEME_TOKENS_CSS`), so Tailwind utilities WIN at equal
specificity. The fix in ζ.2 was to REMOVE conflicting
Tailwind classes from elements that should be themable
(rather than try to override them with !important or
higher specificity). Future ζ.* phases retrofit
visible surfaces the same way: drop the hardcoded
Tailwind color utility, add the theme-* equivalent.

### Today's dark-mode UX

After this ship, on `/preflight` you can:
1. Click the sun icon in the top-right → page flips to
   dark.
2. Reload → still dark (localStorage remembered).
3. Visit on a fresh browser with system dark mode → starts
   dark by default.
4. Click again → flips back to light + persists.

Other 14 consoles still light-only (markers + class
migration not yet absorbed). Future ζ.* phases or
buyer-arc polish work can opt them in as needed; the
toggle button still appears on every page (it's a body-
appended fixed element, independent of marker presence)
and operates the `<html data-theme>` attribute — so
absorbing `THEME_TOKENS_CSS` + theme classes elsewhere
will "just work" with no JS changes.

### Tests (20 new)

In `tests/test_dark_mode_zeta2.py`:

1. **TestZeta2DarkModeJs** (11 tests) — `<script>`
   wrapper, namespaced localStorage key
   (`ebible_theme`), prefers-color-scheme media query,
   synchronous `setAttribute('data-theme', 'dark')`,
   `removeAttribute` for light, the three
   `window.ebibleTheme` methods, `themechange` CustomEvent
   with `detail`, toggle button id pin, idempotent
   insertion (`getElementById` check), aria-label,
   try/catch around localStorage.
2. **TestZeta2ApplyDesignSystem** (4 tests) —
   substitution, no-op on missing marker, idempotency,
   prior markers (HEADER_NAV_LINKS, THEME_TOKENS_CSS,
   BUYER_ARC_POLISH_CSS) still resolve.
3. **TestZeta2PreflightWired** (5 tests) — marker
   substituted, JS appears BEFORE `</head>` (FOAUC
   guard), body uses theme-bg-page + theme-text, header
   uses theme-bg-surface + theme-border, no residual
   `bg-slate-50` in the `<body>` opener (cascade-
   collision guard).

### What ζ.4 inherits

ζ.4 typography upgrade is the next phase. Tokens to add:
`--font-stack-body`, `--font-stack-mono`, `--font-size-base`,
`--leading-normal`. ψ.13's `BTN_*` / `STATUS_*` Tailwind

## 2026-05-11 — session — Δ.10 schema migration framework (Month 1 foundation #6 — closes Month 1, unblocks Track L)

**Phases shipped:** Δ.10 (schema migration framework for
corpus_index SQLite db).
**Test delta:** +26 (`tests/test_migrations_delta10.py`,
5 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### Renumber note (Δ.10 was free)

The original "Δ.10 attribution_audit index-back" was
retired in the ψ.37-E session — investigation found it
already shipped as Δ.3 + Δ.3.1 (no new work needed). The
retirement explicitly did NOT consume the number, leaving
Δ.10 free for the schema-migration-framework slot named in
PROPOSAL_FEATURE_LANDSCAPE §7 / Track L. This ship claims
the slot per §5 sticky-phase rule.

### What shipped

Four pieces wire a minimal migration runner into the
project's only SQLite database (corpus_index):

1. **`scripts/core/migrations.py`** — declarative list:

   ```python
   MIGRATIONS: list[tuple[int, str, str]] = [
       (1, "notes_baseline", _M1_NOTES_BASELINE),
   ]
   ```

   Each entry is `(version, name, sql)`. Versions must
   be strictly increasing positive ints; the runner
   enforces this at import time via
   `migrate._validate_migrations()`. Migration #1's SQL
   is byte-equal to the previous inline `_SCHEMA`
   (notes table + 4 indexes; `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`
   throughout for idempotency).

2. **`scripts/core/migrate.py`** — the runner. Public:
   - `apply_pending(conn)` — applies every migration
     with version > HEAD in order. Per-migration
     transaction (`with conn:`); a failing migration
     rolls back AND aborts the chain (later migrations
     don't run). Records each successful apply in
     `schema_migrations` (version PK, name, applied_at
     ISO-8601 UTC). Returns list of newly-applied
     `(version, name)` tuples.
   - `current_version(conn)` — `MAX(version)` from
     `schema_migrations`, or 0 if the table doesn't
     exist yet (pristine DB).
   - `pending(conn)` — read-only preview of what
     `apply_pending` would do next.
   - `_validate_migrations(items=None)` — checks the
     monotonicity + positivity + name invariants.
     Defaults to the live MIGRATIONS list; tests pass
     explicit lists to verify rejection paths.

   Implementation note: imports `migrations` as a module
   (not as a name) so test monkeypatches of
   `migrations.MIGRATIONS` reach the runner. Importing
   the bound name would snapshot it at module-load time
   and defeat patches.

3. **`scripts/core/corpus_index.py` rewired** — the
   `rebuild()` path now calls
   `migrate.apply_pending(conn)` in place of the inline
   `conn.executescript(_SCHEMA)`. `_SCHEMA` is retained
   as a back-compat alias pointing at migration #1's
   SQL string, so any external import (none observed
   in the current codebase, but the contract was
   public-facing) keeps working.

4. **`scripts/run_migrations.py`** — standalone CLI for
   ad-hoc applies + introspection:

   ```
   python scripts/run_migrations.py             # apply pending
   python scripts/run_migrations.py --dry-run   # list pending
   python scripts/run_migrations.py --current   # print HEAD
   python scripts/run_migrations.py --db <path> # target a file
   ```

   Exit codes match the other audit scripts (0=ok or
   already at HEAD, 1=migration failed, 2=invalid args
   or DB missing on a read intent).

### Schema status today

After this ship, `corpus_index.connection()` returns a
DB whose `schema_migrations` table contains one row:

```
version | name             | applied_at
--------+------------------+------------------------------
   1    | notes_baseline   | <ISO-8601 UTC at first rebuild>
```

A future Δ.12 (FTS5) ship just appends `(2, "fts5_notes",
"CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ...")` to MIGRATIONS — no rebuild
of the framework needed, no `_SCHEMA` constant to edit.

The AUDIT_2026-05-11 §6 proposal called this "ω.36
sonarqube CI gate" but **ω.36 was already consumed earlier
same day** by the path-tagged fingerprint cache (multiplier
3.0 → 1.4). Per CLAUDE_PROJECT_RULES §5 "Letter assignments
are sticky — a feature lives with one letter forever",
this work ships as **ω.47** (next free ω-slot after
ω.37/.38 pre-commit + CI and the ω.39-46 range already
assigned in PROPOSAL_FEATURE_LANDSCAPE.md §7).

### What shipped

Three pieces wire SonarCloud's quality gate into the
project's existing /preflight dashboard alongside
`rules_compliance` + `schema_compliance` (per AUDIT
§6.624):

1. **`sonar-project.properties`** — SonarCloud config:
   - `sonar.organization=bridge4kaladin-collab`
   - `sonar.projectKey=bridge4kaladin-collab_yhwh-bible-platform`
     (SonarCloud's standard `<org>_<github-repo>` convention)
   - `sonar.sources=scripts` (only the Python production
     tree; `content/notes/*.py` is data per pyproject.toml)
   - `sonar.tests=tests`
   - `sonar.python.version=3.10,3.11,3.12,3.13,3.14`
     (matches the ω.38 CI matrix)
   - Exclusions mirror .gitignore + ruff's `extend-exclude`:
     `__pycache__`, `.backups`, `content/notes`,
     `content/translations`, `content/sources`,
     `content/candidates`, `epub_working`, `exports`,
     `builds`, `kings_session`, `source_archive`,
     `assets`, `_audit_state.json`
   - `sonar.scm.provider=git` + `sonar.sourceEncoding=UTF-8`

2. **`scripts/check_sonarqube.py`** — Tier-3 meta-tool
   (~250 lines) wrapping `sonar api get
   /api/qualitygates/project_status`. Public API:
   - `check_quality_gate() -> dict` — returns
     `{"status": "pass"|"warn"|"fail"|"skip", "message":
     str, "details": dict}`. In-process callable so the
     preflight aggregator skips the subprocess hop.
   - `main(argv=None) -> int` — CLI entry; standard
     audit-script exit-code map (0=pass, 1=fail,
     2=warn/skip). `--json` flag emits the dict raw.

   Status semantics:
   - **pass** — gate status `OK`
   - **fail** — gate status `ERROR` (real findings)
   - **warn** — gate status `WARN`, `NONE` (no analysis
     yet), 404 (project not yet on SonarCloud), timeout,
     or non-JSON response
   - **skip** — `sonar-project.properties` missing,
     `sonar.projectKey` unset, or `sonar` CLI absent

3. **`sonarqube_quality_gate` preflight check** — appended
   to `scripts/api/preflight.py::_compute_preflight_uncached()`.
   Lazy-imports `check_sonarqube.check_quality_gate` and
   wraps the call in a broad `except` so a runtime failure
   (network outage, unexpected upstream change, etc.)
   surfaces as `warn` rather than breaking the dashboard.
   Surfaces in /api/preflight + /preflight UI with `id:
   sonarqube_quality_gate, name: SonarCloud quality gate,
   jump_to: /preflight`.

### Live state today

The check returns **warn — "no SonarCloud analysis run
yet"**. The SonarCloud project DOES exist (CLI didn't

### Post-ship: SonarScanner install + Auto Analysis discovery

Mid-session the user offered a sonar-cli source folder at
`C:\Users\bogda\Documents\sonarqube-cli-0.12.0.1512`; that
was the upstream source repo for the same `sonar` CLI
already installed — no install needed. **SonarScanner CLI**
(the heavyweight static analyzer, separate tool) is what's
actually needed to populate the quality gate. Installed
**v8.1.0.6389** to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sonar-scanner\`:
- Downloaded the official Windows x64 zip (~55 MB) from
  `binaries.sonarsource.com/Distribution/sonar-scanner-cli/`.
- Verified: `sonar-scanner.bat --version` reports
  `SonarScanner CLI 8.1.0.6389 / Java 21.0.9 Adoptium /
  Windows 11 10.0 amd64`.

Generated a SonarCloud User Token via `sonar api post
/api/user_tokens/generate` (PowerShell quote-mangling
needed working around — used Bash with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`)
and ran the first scan. **Scanner failed with:**

> ERROR You are running manual analysis while Automatic
> Analysis is enabled. Please consider disabling one or
> the other.

**Discovery**: the SonarCloud project has **Automatic
Analysis enabled** — SonarCloud watches the linked GitHub
repo and runs scans automatically on every push, blocking
manual-scanner runs to avoid duplicate paths. This is
actually the better posture for this project: no
CI scanner step needed, no manual scans needed; pushes
populate the gate.

**Cleanup post-discovery**:
- Revoked the temporary scanner token
  (`yhwh-scanner-2026-05-11`) via `sonar api post
  /api/user_tokens/revoke`.
- Wiped the token cache file (`/tmp/yhwh-sonar-token`).
- SonarScanner stays installed for future Auto-Analysis-off
  scenarios (e.g., a developer wanting to scan a feature
  branch before pushing).

**`scripts/check_sonarqube.py` hint message refined** for
the `NONE`-gate-status case: now mentions both paths (push
triggers Auto Analysis vs manual `sonar-scanner` when Auto
is off). The test that pins this hint stays green
(matcher accepts either of two substrings).

### User out-of-band step (revised)

The gate will flip from warn → pass/fail **automatically**
on your next `./save.cmd` (which pushes to GitHub). No
manual scanner run required. After the push:
- Watch Auto Analysis at `https://sonarcloud.io/project/
  overview?id=bridge4kaladin-collab_yhwh-bible-platform`
- /preflight check will reflect the new gate status on
  next dashboard refresh (the lru_cache invalidates when
  any tracked yaml/notes file mtime changes; manual cache-
  clear via `/api/preflight?nocache=1` is available too)
- If you want manual scans, disable Auto Analysis under
  the project's Administration > Analysis Method settings,
  then run `sonar-scanner` from the repo root.

### Mid-ship regression caught + fixed

During the full-suite verify pass, `TestEditionMeta::
test_preflight_returns_structured_checks` failed:
the existing preflight contract pins every check's
`details` field as a `list` AND `status` as
`pass`/`warn`/`fail` (no `skip`). My initial sonarqube
wire-up passed a `dict` for `details` and could yield
`skip`. Two-line fix in the wire-up: map `skip → warn`
and wrap the info dict as a single-element list (with
`failed_conditions` expanded to a list of `{metricKey,
status}` items when present). Pinned both shape
requirements in `TestOmega47PreflightWired::
test_sonarqube_check_has_required_shape` so a future
re-introduction can't pass silently.

## 2026-05-11 — session — ω.38 GitHub Actions CI (Month 1 foundation #5 — Track B developer experience)

**Phases shipped:** ω.38 (CI workflow + obsolete-template removal).
**Test delta:** +20 (`tests/test_ci_omega38.py`, 6 test classes).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### What shipped

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the project's first
project-tailored GitHub Actions workflow. Mirrors the
locally-enforced contract (`.githooks/pre-commit` +
`dev/git-hooks/pre-commit`) so a green CI run guarantees the
fresh-clone gate would have passed too.

**Two jobs:**

1. **`lint`** (ubuntu-latest × Python 3.12) — installs runtime
   deps + dev tools (ruff, mypy, vulture, pip-audit), then
   runs the full audit chain in pre-commit order:
   - `ruff format --check .`
   - `ruff check .`
   - `python scripts/lint_rules.py` (Tier-3 preflight; 11 checks)
   - `python scripts/audit_deps.py` (pip-audit CVE gate)
   - `python scripts/audit_dead_code.py` (vulture sweep)
   - `python scripts/audit_types.py` (mypy on scripts/core/)
   - `python scripts/audit_caches.py` (@lru_cache audit)

2. **`test`** — pytest matrix across:
   - ubuntu-latest × {3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14}
   - windows-latest × {3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13}
   - macos-latest × 3.12 (trimmed for runner cost)

   Runs `pytest -n auto --dist=loadfile -v --maxfail=10` —
   `loadfile` distribution keeps the YAML-mutator monolith
   tests (`tests/test_scripts.py`) on one worker per
   pyproject.toml's recommendation. `fail-fast: false` so a
   single Python-version breakage doesn't mask others.

**Workflow-wide env:**
- `PYTHONUTF8=1` — required on Windows runners or 72 tests
  fail on cp1252 decoding errors at byte 0x9d. Project memory
  reproduces this reliably.
- `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` — paired safety net for stdout/stderr.

**Concurrency control:** new pushes on the same ref cancel
in-flight runs (saves Actions minutes on noisy PR branches).

**Trigger surface:** push to main, PRs to main, plus
`workflow_dispatch` for manual re-runs after transient
runner failures.

### Obsolete file removed

`.github/workflows/python-package.yml` — GitHub's default
template (Python 3.9-3.11, flake8) was misaligned with this
project (Python target 3.10+, ruff). Replaced by ci.yml.
`.github/workflows/python-publish.yml` left alone — it's a
separate PyPI release flow (currently unused; ξ-5 keeps
requirements.txt-only setup) but doesn't conflict with CI.

### Tests (20 new)

In `tests/test_ci_omega38.py`:

1. **TestOmega38CiWorkflowExists** (3 tests) — file presence,
   YAML parses, top-level `name:` set.
2. **TestOmega38CiWorkflowTriggers** (3 tests) — push to main,
   PR to main, workflow_dispatch all present. Robust to YAML's
   bare-`on:` → Python `True` quirk.
3. **TestOmega38CiWorkflowEnv** (2 tests) — PYTHONUTF8=1 and
   PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 set workflow-wide (not per-job).
4. **TestOmega38CiLintChain** (5 tests) — every step from the
   pre-commit chain is invoked (ruff format/check + lint_rules
   + 4 audit scripts) AND every required dev tool is installed
   in the lint job (so audits don't silently rc=2-skip).
5. **TestOmega38CiTestMatrix** (5 tests) — three OSes present,
   3.10 floor + modern (3.12+) version present, pytest with
   `-n auto --dist=loadfile`, fail-fast: false.
6. **TestOmega38CiObsoleteRemoved** (2 tests) —
   `python-package.yml` is gone; `ci.yml` is canonical.

Pinning rationale: this workflow is the only enforcement gate
on `main` for contributors whose fresh clone hasn't activated
the pre-commit hook (`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`).
Drift here is silent — the maintainer keeps seeing green
checks while coverage degrades — so every requirement gets
an explicit assertion.

Per **PROPOSAL_FEATURE_LANDSCAPE.md §6** the v1.1 sequence
after slice #3 (ψ.36-A) was: ω.36 sonarqube (deferred until

## 2026-05-11 — session — ψ.36-A per-edition matrix endpoint (v1.1 slice #3 — lazy-load data-API foundation)

**Phases shipped:** ψ.36-A (the data-API side of matrix
lazy-load).
**Test delta:** +8 (TestApiMatrixForEditionShape +
TestApiMatrixForEditionParity + TestApiMatrixForEditionRoute
+ TestApiMatrixForEditionErrors).
**Linter delta:** 11/11 clean.

### What shipped

`scripts/web.py::api_matrix_for_edition(edition_id)` — a new
GET endpoint at `/api/matrix/edition/<edition_id>`. Returns
the per-edition slot from `/api/matrix`'s response plus the
categories + kinds + this-one-edition metadata so the client
can render a standalone view without a second `/api/matrix`
round-trip.

This is the 200K-note ceiling lift's **data foundation**:
today's full `/api/matrix` response (~2 MB on a 51K corpus)
is fine, but at 200K it'd get heavy. With this endpoint, the
matrix UI can fetch progressively (one edition at a time)
when corpus growth justifies it. Existing `/api/matrix`
consumers are unaffected.

Implementation reuses the existing
`_api_matrix_per_edition(m, book_ch_counts)` helper (from
ψ.35-B3) — so the per-edition slot is **byte-identical** to
what the full endpoint returns. Equivalence pinned by
`TestApiMatrixForEditionParity::test_matrix_slot_matches_full_response`
(sweeps every edition).

Route registered in `_REGEX_GET_ROUTES`:
`re.compile(r"^/api/matrix/edition/([a-z0-9_-]+)$")`. Returns
`{"error": "unknown edition: ...", "http": 404}` for unknown
edition ids (standard error-envelope contract; the route
adapter translates to a real 404).

In `tests/test_matrix_lazyload_psi36.py`:

- `TestApiMatrixForEditionShape` (5 tests) — top-level keys
  (edition + categories + kinds + matrix), edition-block
  metadata, categories/kinds lists-of-dicts shape, matrix
  slot 11-key contract, totals > 0 for a real edition.
- `TestApiMatrixForEditionParity` (1 test) — byte-for-byte
  parity with /api/matrix's per-edition slot across every
  edition.
- `TestApiMatrixForEditionRoute` (1 test) — route registered
  in `_REGEX_GET_ROUTES` + regex matches a real edition id.
- `TestApiMatrixForEditionErrors` (1 test) — unknown
  edition → `{"error": "unknown edition: ...", "http": 404}`.

### Deferred to ψ.36-B (UI integration)

The endpoint is shipped; consumer migration in the JS matrix
UI is a separate slice (ψ.36-B) that can land when corpus
growth makes the optimization observable. Today's full-
matrix render is fine.

content, correctly returning `None`.

### Bonus slice: ψ.35-A — Matrix accessor methods foundation

The audit's `ARCH-03` recommendation was to collapse the
`Matrix` dataclass's 5 redundant projections (`enabled`,
`potential`, `per_book` are all derivations of
`per_chapter` + `edition_enabled_kinds`). The full collapse
is a multi-slice refactor (15+ consumers in `scripts/web.py`
need migrating). **ψ.35-A** ships the foundation — four
accessor methods on `Matrix` that derive every projected
view from the canonical store, equivalence-pinned against
the existing fields:

- `m.enabled_count(ed, kind)`     ≡ `m.enabled[ed][kind]`
- `m.potential_count(ed, kind)`   ≡ `m.potential[ed][kind]`
- `m.per_book_count(ed, kind, b)` ≡ `m.per_book[ed][kind][b]`
- `m.chapter_dist(ed, kind, b)`   ≡ `m.per_chapter[ed][kind][b]`

The existing six fields stay populated — **zero consumer
migration in this slice.** Future ψ.35 sub-slices (the
"B-track" of the ψ.35 family — see roadmap below) migrate
consumers one at a time; the final slice removes the
redundant projections.

**+9 tests** in `TestPsi35AAccessorMethods`:

- `test_enabled_count_equivalence` — sweep every (ed, kind)
  pair in both `enabled` and `potential`; method output must
  match stored value, including the disabled-kind = 0 contract
- `test_potential_count_equivalence` — sweep every (ed, kind)
  in `potential`; method output must match
- `test_per_book_count_equivalence` — sweep every (ed, kind,
  book) triple in `per_book`
- `test_chapter_dist_equivalence` — sweep every triple in
  `per_chapter`; the entire `{chapter: count}` dict must
  match
- `test_chapter_dist_returns_defensive_copy` — mutating the
  returned dict must not bleed back into the cached matrix
- `test_enabled_count_returns_zero_for_disabled_kind` —
  pin the explicit contract: for any kind NOT in
  `edition_enabled_kinds[ed]`, `enabled_count` returns 0
  even when `potential_count > 0`
- `test_accessor_handles_unknown_edition` — unknown ed →
  every accessor returns 0 / {}
- `test_accessor_handles_unknown_kind` — same for unknown kind
- `test_accessor_methods_are_bound` — pin the method-on-
  dataclass shape (instance methods, not staticmethods)

### Roadmap — future ψ.35 sub-slices (NOT shipped yet)

The full ψ.35 collapse will roll out as a multi-slice
sequence. Each downstream slice will:

- Migrate one cohesive consumer cluster from raw-field
  reads (e.g. `m.enabled.get(ed, {}).get(kind, 0)`) to the
  matching accessor (`m.enabled_count(ed, kind)`).
- Add tests pinning the consumer's behaviour against the
  new API (same as ω.35-B.* tests pinned each topic
  cluster's extraction).
- Ship under a sub-tag like `ψ.35-B1` (snapshot console
  consumers), `ψ.35-B2` (preflight / covers / customize),
  etc. The exact decomposition is publisher-led.

The terminating slice (provisionally tagged `ψ.35-Final`)
will remove the redundant `enabled`, `potential`, and
`per_book` fields from `Matrix` and become a small
cache-footprint improvement; the `per_chapter` field stays
as the canonical store.

### Bonus slice: ψ.35-B1 — Matrix CLI migration + dict accessors

The first **consumer-migration** slice of the ψ.35 family.
ψ.35-A added scalar accessor methods; ψ.35-B1 (a) adds two
dict-returning accessors so consumers that need the whole-
edition `{kind: count}` map have a method-based path, and
(b) migrates `scripts/matrix.py` (the CLI tool) — the
first concrete consumer to move off raw-field reads.

**New accessors on `Matrix`:**

- `m.enabled_kinds_dict(ed)`   ≡ `m.enabled.get(ed, {})`
- `m.potential_kinds_dict(ed)` ≡ `m.potential.get(ed, {})`

Both derive from `per_chapter` + `edition_enabled_kinds`,
returning only kinds with non-zero counts (matching the
stored projection's shape — zero-count kinds are absent,
not stored as 0). Future ψ.35 sub-slices will add similar
dict accessors for `per_book[ed][kind]` if needed; for now
the per-book whole-dict shape isn't actually consumed
anywhere outside `api_matrix`'s JSON response (which stays
on the stored projection for the moment — its migration is
its own slice).

**Consumer migrated:** `scripts/matrix.py` (the CLI tool —
`python scripts/matrix.py` for the category/kind/edition
tables). Five call sites moved from raw-field reads to
the accessor API:

- `m.enabled[ed_id].get(kind_code, 0)` (line 107) →
  `m.enabled_count(ed_id, kind_code)`
- `m.potential[ed_id].get(kind_code, 0)` (line 108) →
  `m.potential_count(ed_id, kind_code)`
- `m.potential[ed_id].values()` for the "filtered out"
  delta row (line 71) →
  `m.potential_kinds_dict(ed_id).values()`
- `m.enabled[edition_id]` for the per-edition detail view
  (line 134) → `m.enabled_kinds_dict(edition_id)`
- `m.potential[edition_id]` (line 135) →
  `m.potential_kinds_dict(edition_id)`

Each migration line carries a `# ψ.35-B1 — was: …` comment
so the original raw-field expression is preserved in source
for future readers.

### Bonus slice: ψ.35-Final — projection fields auto-derived

The terminating slice of the ψ.35 family. Three changes:

1. **`Matrix` dataclass** — `enabled`, `potential`, and
   `per_book` are now `init=False`. The build pipelines no
   longer pass them in. A new `__post_init__` derives them
   from `per_chapter` + `edition_enabled_kinds` via the
   dict accessor methods, using `object.__setattr__` to
   bypass the frozen-dataclass immutability.

2. **`_compute_matrix_via_file_walk()`** — the
   pre-ψ.35-Final body had a triple-nested loop that built
   `enabled`, `potential`, `per_book`, AND `per_chapter` in
   a single pass. The slim version builds ONLY `per_chapter`;
   the three derived dicts get auto-materialized in
   `__post_init__`. ~30 lines of loop body deleted.

3. **`corpus_index.compute_matrix_indexed()`** — same
   simplification; same ~25-line reduction.

**API surface preserved.** Every existing consumer that
does `m.enabled[ed_id]` / `m.potential[ed_id]` /
`m.per_book[ed_id]` continues working unchanged because
the field name is still present — only its *source* moved
from caller-passed to derived-in-post-init.

**Storage at the build site drops** by 3 dict-of-dicts
allocations + the inner summation loops that populated
them. The per-Matrix-instance footprint is unchanged —
__post_init__ materializes the projections once and stores
them via object.__setattr__. (A future cleanup could swap
the materialized fields for `@cached_property` to defer
the build cost; today's call sites all read all three
projections, so the laziness wouldn't save anything in
practice.)

**Δ.4 equivalence still holds.** Both build pipelines
(`_compute_matrix_via_file_walk` and `compute_matrix_indexed`)
go through the same `__post_init__`, so their outputs are
guaranteed equivalent for the same per_chapter +
edition_enabled_kinds inputs. Pinned by
`test_delta4_equivalence_still_holds_post_psi35_final` in
the new test class.

**+6 tests** in `TestPsi35FinalProjectionsAutoDerived`:

- `test_projection_fields_still_accessible` — API surface
  pin: `m.enabled[ed]` / `m.potential[ed]` / `m.per_book[ed]`
  still return dicts for every edition in the live matrix.
- `test_projection_fields_are_init_false` — dataclass
  shape pin: the three derived fields have `init=False`,
  the three canonical-source fields have `init=True`.
- `test_matrix_constructible_from_canonical_only` —
  synthetic Matrix with only the canonical-source kwargs
  builds and auto-derives the expected projections.
- `test_disabled_kind_excluded_from_auto_derived_enabled` —
  the disabled-kind contract holds: a kind in per_chapter
  but NOT in edition_enabled_kinds is in `potential` but
  not `enabled`.
- `test_build_pipelines_no_longer_pass_projection_kwargs` —
  source-scan of scripts/core/matrix.py + corpus_index.py
  confirms `enabled=enabled,` / `potential=potential,` /
  `per_book=per_book,` are absent from `Matrix(...)`
  construction.
- `test_delta4_equivalence_still_holds_post_psi35_final` —
  the file-walk and indexed paths still produce equivalent
  Matrix objects across all six fields after the migration.

  tests, shared SQLite path across workers)
